messages:
alex: quick check — running into a weird streaming/redirect auth issue in the kotlin client. Using OkHttp + Jackson shaded into the client artifact. If a request 302s we lose Authorization header and the server closes the stream mid-token. Anyone seen this?

priya: yup. OkHttp will drop the header on cross-host redirects by default. If it's same-host it should keep it, but network vs application interceptors matter. Are you using addInterceptor or addNetworkInterceptor? :thinking_face:

alex: addInterceptor (we add auth header in a single interceptor). Example: 
```kotlin
client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $TOKEN")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .build()
```

jamie: for redirects the recommendation is to add the header via a network interceptor so it runs after redirects are handled, or set client.followRedirects(false) and handle 3xx yourself. network interceptor sees the exact network request.

morgan: also check followSslRedirects vs followRedirects depending on protocol changes. And if the redirect is to a different host, okHttp intentionally drops auth for security.

alex: good call — it's same host but different path. I switched to addNetworkInterceptor and the immediate 302 -> stream close still happens (server terminates chunked stream). Could be related to Jackson/Gson shading — stacktrace shows NoSuchMethodError around com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ObjectMapper.findAndRegisterModules

kyle: shading can rename packages; if you relocated jackson during shading but another dependency expects the original package, you get NoSuchMethod. Are you using the kotlin-module and relocating only jackson-databind but not jackson-module-kotlin?

priya: also check if the runtime loads two versions of jackson via classloader (shadowed + platform). In our builds we've kept jackson packages unrelocated and instead shaded only our internal helpers. That avoids reflection method resolution issues with jackson-module-kotlin.

alex: stacktrace pasted: 
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper.findAndRegisterModules()Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ObjectMapper;
  at com.example.lib.JsonUtilsKt.setupMapper(JsonUtilsKt.kt:34)
  at com.example.lib.ApiClient.create(ApiClient.kt:78)
```

jamie: that line suggests the compiled code expected that method (added in jackson 2.2x?). Make sure runtime jackson version matches compile-time. If you shaded to an older version you'll see that.

morgan: temporary test — run with JVM arg -Djava.system.class.loader to ensure single loader? maybe overkill. Simpler: run `mvn dependency:tree` / `gradle dependencies` and grep jackson artifacts.

kyle: for okhttp streaming and redirects, another workaround is to use request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token) inside an authenticator on 401 rather than interceptor for redirects. But that changes semantics.

alex: thanks. Plan: 1) audit deps to confirm jackson versions, 2) revert relocation for jackson-module-kotlin, 3) switch to addNetworkInterceptor for auth header if needed, and 4) repro streaming with followRedirects(false) to see raw 302 body. I'll open a draft PR with the shading revert and add a reproducer test.

priya: SGTM. ping me on the PR, happy to review. Also add a unit test that asserts no NoSuchMethodError on startup — CI should catch it.

deploy-bot: build/1857 started by alex — gradle build (kotlin-client)

jamie: one more note — if the server sends a 302 with transfer-encoding: chunked and then closes, OkHttp might surface that as EOFException when reading the stream. That can be legitimate server behaviour; verifying headers + redirect handling is key.

alex: noted. I'll attach logs from local run to the PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
